artboards.name: home-page
artboards.role: Desktop (1440px) marketing home page for Forno Rosso, a wood-fired pizzeria: global header with primary nav + cart indicator, hero, delivery banner, featured menu grid, brand-story section, and footer. The linked Figma node is a single top-level FRAME (not a CANVAS with sibling artboards) — header/hero/delivery-banner/featured-section/story-section/footer are sections within this one screen, not separate artboards.

brand_red.usage: logo badge, active nav text + underline, primary CTA fill, price text, section eyebrow text

brand_green.usage: delivery-banner background, story-section eyebrow text, bolded ETA value inside header delivery estimate

ink.usage: header/hero/footer dark background, body heading text on light surfaces, Add to Order button fill

surface_white.usage: menu card background, text on dark backgrounds

muted_text.usage: menu card descriptions, story-section body copy

open_questions.detail: CartIndicatorButton (6:22) shows a static badge with count '3'. The design has no drawn state for an empty cart (0 items) — this is exactly the kind of undrawn state the review pass is meant to flag, and it's central to this story's cart-indicator feature.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Hide the numeric badge entirely when count is 0 (bare cart icon only); show the numeral for any count >= 1.

options.label: Hide badge at 0 items — common e-commerce convention, avoids a visually 'full' looking icon with no items
Always render the badge, showing '0' when the cart is empty

open_questions.detail: The Figma frame is one static capture of a 2786px-tall page; it gives no signal on whether the header should stay fixed/sticky while the rest of the page (hero, delivery banner, featured grid, story, footer) scrolls underneath.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Implement SiteHeader as sticky to the top of the viewport on scroll, since persistent access to nav + cart indicator is the point of a header on a long scrolling commerce page.

options.label: Sticky/fixed header, always visible while scrolling
Static header that scrolls away with the page content

open_questions.detail: The 'Authentic Neapolitan Woodfired' eyebrow pill (6:27) uses a fire-extinguisher glyph (node 6:679) — visually confirmed in the rendered PNG. A flame/fire icon would better match the copy about wood-fired ovens; this looks like a mis-picked icon in the source icon set.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Implement the icon exactly as drawn (fire-extinguisher glyph name) since the rendered PNG is authoritative for visuals; do not silently substitute a flame icon.

open_questions.topic: Duplicate cart entry points in the header
open_questions.detail: The center PrimaryNav includes a plain text 'Cart' link (6:18) in addition to the circular CartIndicatorButton with item-count badge (6:22) on the far right. Both plausibly point at cart/checkout functionality.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Treat the nav 'Cart' text link as a standard navigation entry to the full cart/checkout page, and the right-side CartIndicatorButton as a persistent glanceable indicator (and likely trigger for a cart preview/drawer); both route to the same cart destination but serve different UX roles.

open_questions.topic: MenuCard title truncation on long names
open_questions.detail: Longer pizza names ('Funghi Selvatici & Tartufo', 'Prosciutto Crudo e Rucola') appear visually truncated with an ellipsis in the rendered PNG, even though the underlying Figma text node is set to HUG sizing (untruncated).
open_questions.arc_assumption: Apply single-line CSS truncation (text-overflow: ellipsis, white-space: nowrap) to the MenuCard title so long names don't wrap and break the card's fixed height, matching the PNG's truncated appearance.

open_questions.detail: 'Estimated delivery: 30 mins', the cart count '3', 'Average ETA: 25-35 Min', and 'Piping Hot Guaranteed' are literal strings in the Figma file with no indication of how they'd be sourced from real order/delivery data.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Model these as component props (not literal hardcoded strings) so they can be wired to real delivery/ETA/cart data at integration time; the Figma copy is treated as placeholder content for layout purposes only.

open_questions.detail: 'Estimated delivery: 30 mins' (6:21) uses two different colors/weights within a single Figma text node (white/regular label + brand-green/semibold value) via a character style override — a single plain-string prop can't express this.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Give DeliveryEtaLabel a `label` and a `value` prop (two spans) rather than one string, so each can be styled independently in code.
